name: Fucked Up
label: Matador
lede: Fucked Up came out of Toronto hardcore with stage names, a blizzard of seven-inches and a screamer called Pink Eyes. Then came flutes, a Polaris Prize, a 77-minute rock opera and a zodiac cycle that took twenty years to finish.

eras.title: Hiding behind stage names
eras.text: Fucked Up started in Toronto in 2001 as a hardcore band whose members used aliases (10,000 Marbles, Concentration Camp, Mustard Gas, Pink Eyes) and put out singles by the handful. The records looked like occult pamphlets, and the songs kept getting longer.

years.h: Fucked Up starts in Toronto, and nobody uses a real name
years.p: [[Mike Haliechuk|06275171-c023-495b-98d7-fac7671fed48]] (10,000 Marbles), [[Josh Zucker|16ca8eac-3b25-45d0-8535-c1c46d5cf08d]] (Concentration Camp), Sandy Miranda (Mustard Gas) and drummer [[Chris Colohan|f1494c0a-331d-45dd-a51c-6c43d43ccc69]] start the band; [[Damian Abraham|a718a47a-e63c-4c59-8b98-5df130e57f64]], Pink Eyes, joins before the demo.
years.xp: Zucker started on vocals before moving to guitar once Abraham came in. [[Jonah Falco|62eca584-0333-4bbd-be97-b71d04cc230f]], Mr. Jo, replaced Colohan on drums, and Colohan went on to front [[Cursed|16d6213e-2138-4a41-8ba5-acf8bd8fc69a]].

years.h: The first 7-inch, No Pasaran, opens a run of singles
years.p: Fucked Up's first single, No Pasaran, is followed within a year by The Police (March 2003) and Baiting the Public (May 2003).

years.h: Epics in Minutes gathers the singles on one CD
years.p: A CD compilation rounds up Fucked Up's singles, the same year the band self-released the Looking for Gold 12-inch in runs of 300 and 400 copies.

eras.title: A debut longer than most careers
eras.text: The first album ran 72 minutes, and the band started a series of long singles named for the Chinese zodiac that would take twenty years to finish. On Canadian TV, their shows started wrecking studios.

years.h: One long song per zodiac sign, starting with the Dog
years.p: The Year of the Dog 12-inch launches Fucked Up's Zodiac series, one long piece per sign of the Chinese zodiac. The last installment is announced in 2025.

years.h: Hidden World runs 72 minutes, and Exclaim! has it at No. 1
years.p: Jade Tree puts it out on CD and Deranged presses a double LP. Exclaim! names it the best punk album of the year.
years.xp: [[Owen Pallett|6d394418-a565-4c16-9dec-f5a89e213cde]], then recording as Final Fantasy, plays violin. Guest vocalists include [[Alexisonfire|bc1c8f3f-6f36-4086-a470-87ed813dd429]]'s George Pettit and [[Dallas Green|06b65c62-b894-45ec-88f4-b7d689851e35]], Chris Colohan, and Ben Cook of No Warning, a year before he joined.

q: Damian Abraham, on the washroom show
yt: Twice Born, the MTV Live washroom show, 2008
years.h: MTV Canada bans moshing after Fucked Up plays the studio
years.p: Introduced as 'Effed Up' on MTV Live in Toronto, the band plays Baiting the Public while the crowd does about $2,000 in damage and cuts Damian Abraham's forehead.
years.xp:
They came back on October 9, 2008, and played in the MTV Live men's washroom. Band and fans tore out the ceiling, spray-painted the walls and knocked over amps and a prop motorcycle; the show was stopped after one song. MTV hadn't known the destruction was planned.

Abraham described it on his blog as "fucking out of control terrifying."

years.h: Ben Cook goes from guest vocalist to rhythm guitarist
years.p: Cook, of No Warning, sang on Hidden World as a guest. Now he joins Fucked Up as rhythm guitarist and backing vocalist.

years.h: Nelly Furtado and David Cross sing on a Christmas single
years.p: Fucked Up's holiday single David Christmas features [[Nelly Furtado|13655113-cd16-4b43-9dca-cadbbf26ee05]], [[Davey Havok|0d7bf43a-d747-4c8b-bc4c-927d9a7fe03a]], David Cross, Shenae Grimes and Faris Badwan.

years.h: The New York Times prints them as asterisks
years.p: Fucked Up are filmed in New York for Richard Roepnack's film Burn. The New York Times reviews it kindly but prints the band's name as asterisks.

eras.title: The flutes win Polaris
eras.text: The second album brought in French horns, flutes and organ, and a hardcore band landed on critics' lists everywhere. Fucked Up sued Rolling Stone, played for twelve hours on the Bowery, and took the Polaris Prize.

years.h: Fucked Up and Xiu Xiu take Rolling Stone and Camel to court
years.p: Fucked Up and [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]] sue Rolling Stone and Camel cigarettes over an Indie Rock Universe ad they say made them look like cigarette supporters.
years.xp: A California appeals court threw out the suit on January 28, 2010, on free speech and press grounds.

years.h: Keith Morris takes the mic for Circle Jerks songs in Austin
years.p: At Austin's Mess With Texas fest, [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] of the [[Circle Jerks|22995eba-1238-4b4f-a937-ac2c5767ab9f]] sings Backed Against the Wall, Beverly Hills and Black Flag's Nervous Breakdown with Fucked Up.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Chemistry of Common Life
years.h: The flutes arrive on The Chemistry of Common Life
years.p: Recorded in Toronto with producer Jon Drew, Fucked Up's Matador debut is 52 minutes of hardcore with flute, French horn and organ. Pitchfork gives it 8.8.
years.xp: The title comes from a book by James F. W. Johnston about the hallucinogenic properties of mushrooms and plants, and the cover shows Manhattanhenge. Members of [[Vivian Girls|d0676301-7ffc-4ff6-8b38-f8aeb8553115]] and Dallas Green sing on it.

years.h: Twelve hours on the Bowery, with Moby and Dinosaur Jr. dropping in
years.p: To mark the album, Fucked Up play for twelve hours on the Bowery. Guests include [[Ezra Koenig|6900fc31-d624-422c-9aa8-b3e6c8cc25ea]], [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]], [[John Joseph|64581915-b050-4a79-b1bf-29fdf6005093]] of the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]], Les Savy Fav and [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]
years.xp: The October 14 show marked the release of The Chemistry of Common Life a week earlier. Guests besides those named included members of Endless Boogie.

years.h: The Festival of the Fuck Bands lands in Fucking, Austria
years.p: Four bands with Fuck in the name, Fucked Up, [[Holy Fuck|4342cf80-7c06-4402-a431-457e77310474]], Fuck and [[Fuck Buttons|f4640b20-b76b-40d3-9ffc-a38b6718b273]], play in the Austrian village of Fucking.

years.h: Jello Biafra sings Blitzkrieg Bop with them at the Echoplex
years.p: At the Echoplex in Los Angeles, [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] joins Fucked Up for the Ramones' Blitzkrieg Bop, and Keith Morris repeats his Circle Jerks cameo.

years.h: Damian Abraham says no to a Fox News guest slot
years.p: Fox News wants him as a regular left-wing guest on Red Eye. Host Greg Gutfeld had named The Chemistry of Common Life the best album of 2008.

years.h: A screaming hardcore record takes the Polaris Prize
years.p: The Chemistry of Common Life wins the 2009 Polaris Music Prize for the best Canadian album of the year.

years.h: Do They Know It's Christmas? with Tegan and Sara, Bob Mould and GZA
years.p: Fucked Up's all-star cover, with [[Ezra Koenig|6900fc31-d624-422c-9aa8-b3e6c8cc25ea]], [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]] members and Kevin Drew too, raises money for groups working on Canada's missing and murdered Indigenous women.

eras.title: David gets a rock opera
eras.text: In 2011 Fucked Up made its biggest swing, a 77-minute rock opera set in Thatcher-era England that Spin called the album of the year. They paused, came back at Metallica's festival, and made a record about staying punk as they got older.

yt: Queen of Hearts, live on KEXP
years.h: A Record Store Day comp invents bands from a town that doesn't exist
years.p: The Record Store Day LP David's Town pretends to document bands from Byrdesdale Spa, the made-up late-1970s English town of the next album. [[A.C. Newman|bb40af12-0dfd-4a53-bfe1-666a9e49dfb2]] and [[Danko Jones|ab4721e4-bc37-4bd2-be8c-8f1550152ad6]] sing on it.

q: Really we're talking about my breaking with my girlfriend.
yt: Let Her Rest / Queen of Hearts, live for Pitchfork
years.h: Spin picks a rock opera as the album of 2011
years.p: David Comes to Life has 18 songs and a plot: factory worker David Eliade falls for activist Veronica Boisson, and it ends with a bombing gone wrong.
years.xp:
The story is told by unreliable narrators, with the villain Octavio St. Laurent controlling the tale until Vivian Benson reveals what really happened. Damian Abraham said the characters let the band hide personal things, including a breakup.

It reached No. 83 on the Billboard 200 and was shortlisted for the 2012 Polaris Prize, which went to [[Feist|a670e05a-cea8-4b37-bce9-d82daf1a0fa4]].

years.h: Abraham spends three years hosting MuchMusic's The Wedge
years.p: Abraham starts a three-year run hosting MuchMusic's alternative video show The Wedge (2011–2014).

years.h: Anthony Bourdain gets a Jingle Bells on No Reservations
years.p: Fucked Up play Jingle Bells on the Christmas episode of Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations.

years.h: Metallica's festival is where the break ends
years.p: After a hiatus from late 2011, so Damian Abraham could spend time with his family, the band returns at [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]]'s Orion Music + More festival in Atlantic City.

years.h: Glass Boys ends the Matador run
years.p: Fucked Up's last Matador album, recorded partly at Electrical Audio in Chicago, has [[Gord Downie|291eb640-aa58-45e9-a8cb-069d58644b2b]] on The Art of Patrons and [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] on Led by Hand.

years.h: Abraham starts a podcast about how people turned out punk
years.p: Abraham's podcast Turned Out a Punk starts, with musicians and fans telling the story of how they found punk.

eras.title: Ben Cook walks, David comes back
eras.text: After a four-year wait, the longest in their history, Fucked Up moved to Merge with an 82-minute double album that brought back the character David. The zodiac cycle kept turning, and in 2021 the six-piece became five.

years.h: A score recorded in 2011 for a 1928 silent film comes out
years.p: Fucked Up self-release Zanzibar, recorded in 2011 as a soundtrack for Tod Browning's 1928 film West of Zanzibar.

years.h: Merge releases Dose Your Dreams, 82 minutes with David back
years.p: Produced by Mike Haliechuk and Jonah Falco, the double album brings back David. It's Ben Cook's last album with the band and earns a Juno nomination.

years.h: Year of the Horse gets a whole album
years.p: The ninth Zodiac installment, Year of the Horse, arrives as a whole album, self-released.

years.h: After fourteen years, Ben Cook leaves
years.p: Guitarist and singer Ben Cook leaves Fucked Up. Robin Hatch fills his spot on tour.
years.xp: Robin Hatch filled in on guitar for the tour that followed.

eras.title: Twenty-four hours at a time
eras.text: Fucked Up gave themselves a rule: each member gets one day to write and record their part. It produced a run of records, one of them written, recorded and released live on the internet, then gone after a day.

years.h: Each member gets 24 hours to make One Day
years.p: Mike Haliechuk wrote and recorded his guitar parts in one December 2019 session, and the others followed the same rule. The pandemic held the mix until 2022.

years.h: The album that exists for 24 hours
years.p: Fucked Up livestream the making of Who's Got the Time & a Half? over August 6-7, 2024, then put it on Bandcamp for just 24 hours.

years.h: Another Day answers One Day song for song
years.p: Another Day follows the same 24-hour rules, each song matching one on One Day. Someday is surprise-released November 1.

years.h: Dave Nardi joins, and it's a six-piece again
years.p: Dave Nardi joins as rhythm guitarist, making Fucked Up a six-piece again.

years.h: Grass Can Move Stones will close the Zodiac
years.p: Fucked Up announce the end of the series begun in 2006: three LPs covering the Goat, the Monkey and the Rooster.
years.xp: The finale is billed as a ten-part cycle across Year of the Goat (LP), Year of the Monkey (2xLP) and Year of the Rooster (2xLP), almost five hours of music. It follows nine installments released from 2006 to 2021.
